top_signals.title: StanChart Sees Higher Oil Floor as Hormuz Crisis Spreads to Saudi Export Routes
top_signals.summary: Oil prices pulled back but remained elevated ahead of a critical Fed decision on Wednesday, with market expectations shifting towards a prolonged US-Iran conflict. Brent crude for November delivery fell 2.88% at 2:18 p.m. ET, to trade at $105.6 per barrel, while WTI crude for October delivery declined 3.33% to change hands at $102.3/bbl. The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points on Wednesday to a range of 3.75% to 4.00%, its first rate hike since 2023, as policymakers responded to renewed inflationary pressure. top_signals.title: Trump Floats EU Tariffs on Canada Invite, Warsh’s Inflation Fight Calms Market
top_signals.summary:
Global bond yields retreated Thursday as the Federal Reserve’s rate hike and vow to tame inflation calmed a pressured market, leaving traders to look ahead to Friday’s key Bank of Japan decision.

President Donald Trump floated hitting goods imported from the European Union with fresh tariffs or even cutting off some trade if he determined that a push to make Canada a potential associate of the bloc was harmful to the US.

The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards and Guy Johnson. (Source: Bloomberg)
